e-4936.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
e-4936.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(9,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}=3\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}.$
e-4936.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 9,-2,3 \rangle$ and the normal vector of the plane is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 3,-4,7 \rangle.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =⟨9,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z-56 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4937.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
e-4937.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,4,8)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\dfrac{x+3}{-5}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{2}.$
e-4937.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -1,4,8 \rangle.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =⟨-1,4,8⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z-33 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4938.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
e-4938.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x-y+z+13=0$ of the plane $\Pi,$ find an equation of $\Pi$ in the form $(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{n}=0.$
e-4938.worked_solution:
First, from the coefficients in equation of the plane, we get that the normal vector of $\Pi$ is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 2,-1,1 \rangle.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $\Pi$ for $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+z+13 & =0 \\ z & =-2x+y-13\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0,$ we get $z=-13.$ So, the point $P(0,0,-13)$ lies on $\Pi.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 0,0,-13 \rangle.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-13⟩)\cdot ⟨2,-1,1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4939.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
e-4939.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,2,-6)$ and is parallel to the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle -3, 5, 2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 1, 3, -2 \rangle.$
e-4939.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,-6 \rangle.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-16i-4j-14k \\  & =⟨-16,-4,-14⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =⟨-3,2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z-124 & =0 \\ 8x+2y+7z+62 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-2,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=3i+4j-k.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,3,-1⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨3,4,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−2,3,−1) and is perpendicular to the vector n=3i+4j−k.

a
x+3y−4z−17=0
b
4x−3y−z+13=0
c
3x−4y−z+9=0
d
3x+4y−z−7=0
e
4x+3y−z−11=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−2,3,−1⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨3,4,−1⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=⟨−2,3,−1⟩⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩r⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=7.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=73x+4y−z=73x+4y−z−7=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-2,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=3i+4j-k.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,3,-1⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨3,4,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(5,0,−3) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨2,4,−1⟩.

a
x+y−z−18=0
b
5x+y−3z−13=0
c
2x+4y+z+5=0
d
5x−3z−13=0
e
2x+4y−z−13=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨5,0,−3⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨2,4,−1⟩.

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨2,4,−1⟩=⟨5,0,−3⟩⋅⟨2,4,−1⟩r⋅⟨2,4,−1⟩=13.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨2,4,−1⟩=132x+4y−z=132x+4y−z−13=0.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms 2x+4y-z=13 because (5,0,-3)·(2,4,-1)=13. Thus option e is correct. The deliberately submitted option d is incorrect: it does not pass through P and its normal is not parallel to the given vector.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(5,0,-3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,4,-1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨5,0,-3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,4,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,4,-1⟩ & =⟨5,0,-3⟩\cdot ⟨2,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,4,-1⟩ & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,4,-1⟩ & =13 \\ 2x+4y-z & =13 \\ 2x+4y-z-13 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

x+y+3z−5=0
b

c

d

e
2x+2y+z−5=0

decision.explanation: The given vector (2,0,1) is normal to the plane, so 2(x-1)+0(y-0)+(z-3)=0. Simplifying gives 2x+z-5=0, option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5 \\ 2x+z & =5 \\ 2x+z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}

Question 3
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(1,0,3) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨2,0,1⟩.

a
x+y+3z−5=0
b
2x+z−5=0
c
2x−5y+z=0
d
x+3z−5=0
e
2x+2y+z−5=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨1,0,3⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨2,0,1⟩.

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨2,0,1⟩=⟨1,0,3⟩⋅⟨2,0,1⟩r⋅⟨2,0,1⟩=5.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨2,0,1⟩=52x+z=52x+z−5=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5 \\ 2x+z & =5 \\ 2x+z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−1,1,−2) and is perpendicular to the vector n=i+j+3k.

a
x−y+2z−5=0
b
x+y+3z+8=0
c
x+y+3z+5=0
d
x+y+3z+6=0
e
−x+y−2z+6=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−1,1,−2⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨1,1,3⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨1,1,3⟩=⟨−1,1,−2⟩⋅⟨1,1,3⟩r⋅⟨1,1,3⟩=−6.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨1,1,3⟩=−6x+y+3z=−6x+y+3z+6=0.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that x+y+3z=(-1)+1+3(-2)=-6, giving x+y+3z+6=0. Its normal is (1,1,3) and it passes through P, so option d is correct. Option b fails at P.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,1,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=i+j+3k.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-1,1,-2⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨1,1,3⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =⟨-1,1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =-6 \\ x+y+3z & =-6 \\ x+y+3z+6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}

Question 5
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(1,−2,4) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨0,3,−5⟩.

a
3x+y−5z+26=0
b
3y−5z+24=0
c
3y+5z+26=0
d
3y−5z+26=0
e
3y−5z−26=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨1,−2,4⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨0,3,−5⟩.

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨0,3,−5⟩=⟨1,−2,4⟩⋅⟨0,3,−5⟩r⋅⟨0,3,−5⟩=−26

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨0,3,−5⟩=−263y−5z=−263y−5z+26=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b
−3x+4z+1=0
c
−3x+y+4z−1=0
d
3x−5y+2z+1=0
e
−5x+3y+2z+1=0

decision.explanation: The line's direction (3,-5,2) is a normal vector to the plane. Through P(-3,0,4), its equation is 3(x+3)-5y+2(z-4)=0, which simplifies to 3x-5y+2z+1=0, option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,0,4)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨-3,0,4⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,-5,2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,-5,2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =⟨-3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z+1 & =0.\end{aligned}

Question 6

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−3,0,4) and is perpendicular to the line r=[−241]+t[3−52].

a
3x−5y+z+1=0
b
−3x+4z+1=0
c
−3x+y+4z−1=0
d
3x−5y+2z+1=0
e
−5x+3y+2z+1=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨−3,0,4⟩. From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector ⟨3,−5,2⟩. So, the normal vector of the plane is

n=⟨3,−5,2⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨3,−5,2⟩=⟨−3,0,4⟩⋅⟨3,−5,2⟩r⋅⟨3,−5,2⟩=−1.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨3,−5,2⟩=−13x−5y+2z=−13x−5y+2z+1=0.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that the plane's normal is the line's direction (3,-5,2). Since (3,-5,2)·(-3,0,4)=-1, its equation is 3x-5y+2z+1=0, option d. Option a fails at P, giving -4 instead of 0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,0,4)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨-3,0,4⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,-5,2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,-5,2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =⟨-3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(8,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\frac{x+2}{4}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z-2}{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨8,3,-1⟩.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨4,3,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨4,3,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =⟨8,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z-42 & =0.\end{aligned}

Question 7
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(8,3,−1) and is perpendicular to the line x+24=y−13=z−2−1.

a
−2x+y+2z−42=0
b
4x+3y−z−42=0
c
−2x+y+2z=0
d
8x+3y−z−42=0
e
4x+3y−z=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨8,3,−1⟩. From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector ⟨4,3,−1⟩. So, the normal vector of the plane is

n=⟨4,3,−1⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨4,3,−1⟩=⟨8,3,−1⟩⋅⟨4,3,−1⟩r⋅⟨4,3,−1⟩=42

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨4,3,−1⟩=424x+3y−z=424x+3y−z−42=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(8,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\frac{x+2}{4}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z-2}{-1}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨8,3,-1⟩.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨4,3,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨4,3,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =⟨8,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z-42 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,1,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=1 \\ y=-2+4t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,1,0⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨0,4,1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨0,4,1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =⟨2,1,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4 \\ 4y+z & =4 \\ 4y+z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨2,1,0⟩. From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector ⟨0,4,1⟩. So, the normal vector of the plane is

n=⟨0,4,1⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨0,4,1⟩=⟨2,1,0⟩⋅⟨0,4,1⟩r⋅⟨0,4,1⟩=4

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨0,4,1⟩=44y+z=44y+z−4=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,1,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=1 \\ y=-2+4t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,1,0⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨0,4,1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨0,4,1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =⟨2,1,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4 \\ 4y+z & =4 \\ 4y+z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-5,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=3+t \\ y=t \\ z=7-t\end{aligned}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨1,-5,2⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨1,1,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨1,1,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ & =⟨1,-5,2⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ & =-6 \\ x+y-z & =-6 \\ x+y-z+6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 12
?

Given the Cartesian equation 7x+y−3=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,3,0⟩)⋅⟨7,1,0⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,−3,0⟩)⋅⟨7,−1,0⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,6,0⟩)⋅⟨0,7,1⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,−6,0⟩)⋅⟨7,0,1⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,9,0⟩)⋅⟨−7,0,1⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients give the normal vector ⟨7,1,0⟩. The point (0,3,0) lies on the plane since 7(0)+3-3=0. Therefore option a expands to the given equation 7x+y-3=0.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $7x+y-3=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨7,1,0⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x+y-3 & =0 \\ y & =3-7x.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$, we get $y=3.$ Hence, the point $P(0,3,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,3,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,3,0⟩)\cdot ⟨7,1,0⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $7x+y-3=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨7,1,0⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}7x+y-3 & =0 \\ y & =3-7x.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$, we get $y=3.$ Hence, the point $P(0,3,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,3,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,3,0⟩)\cdot ⟨7,1,0⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-3,2,4⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -7\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =19i+7j+k \\  & =⟨19,7,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨19,7,1⟩ & =⟨-3,2,4⟩\cdot ⟨19,7,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨19,7,1⟩ & =-39\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨19,7,1⟩ & =-39 \\ 19x+7y+z & =-39 \\ 19x+7y+z+39 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,0,-3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨-3,2,0⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,0,1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨2,0,-3⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2i+3j \\  & =⟨2,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,3,0⟩ & =⟨2,0,-3⟩\cdot ⟨2,3,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,3,0⟩ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,3,0⟩ & =4 \\ 2x+3y & =4 \\ 2x+3y-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -3 & -6 \\ 0 & 2 & -8\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =36i+16j+4k \\  & =⟨36,16,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =⟨-4,3,5⟩\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =-76\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨36,16,4⟩ & =-76 \\ 36x+16y+4z & =-76 \\ 36x+16y+4z+76 & =0 \\ 9x+4y+z+19 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: AP=(2,3,2) and AQ=(3,6,-1). Their cross product is (-15,8,3), so use normal (15,-8,-3). Its dot product with A is 30+40-3=67, giving 15x-8y-3z-67=0. Substitution confirms all three points satisfy option e.

after.name: Question 20
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(2,-5,1)$, $P(4,-2,3)$ and $Q(5,1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨2,-5,1⟩,\,p=⟨4,-2,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨5,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨4,-2,3⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨5,1,0⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,6,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-15i+8j+3k \\  & =⟨-15,8,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z+67 & =0 \\ 15x-8y-3z-67 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−15,8,3⟩=−67−15x+8y+3z=−67−15x+8y+3z+67=015x−8y−3z−67=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(2,-5,1)$, $P(4,-2,3)$ and $Q(5,1,0).$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨2,-5,1⟩,\,p=⟨4,-2,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨5,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨4,-2,3⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨5,1,0⟩-⟨2,-5,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,6,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-15i+8j+3k \\  & =⟨-15,8,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =⟨4,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-15,8,3⟩ & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z & =-67 \\ -15x+8y+3z+67 & =0 \\ 15x-8y-3z-67 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
